purpose: Manufacturer-manual-grounded menu reference. Menu numbers are panel addresses only when the cited manual explicitly identifies them as such; order is a presentation ordering field, never a keypad shortcut.

nodeShape.label: Exact short menu label
nodeShape.summary: Original concise functional explanation, not long manual quotation

numberingShape.explanation: How this particular menu navigation works

gapShape.title: Specific unresolved point
gapShape.question: A precise question for the owner
gapShape.neededEvidence: Photo of version screen, menu page, manual revision, etc.

coverageShape.confidence: Documented baseline, not a claim of complete firmware emulation

rules: Parent IDs must exist or be null; graph must be acyclic.
Every node must have at least one valid source reference with an exact one-based PDF page.
Separate user, engineer and edition-specific menu roots. State any source-version split plainly.
Do not make manual chapter numbering into menu codes or invent selectable submenus for mere narrative headings.
Configuration value lists may be nodes only when clearly labelled selection/reference; they are not claimed navigable submenus.
Use exact factual short menu names, paraphrase descriptions. Do not reproduce manuals wholesale.
Mark gaps instead of guessing unsupported routes. Keep web research and downloaded source fingerprints reproducible.
No new credentials, default codes, live panel transport or permanent hardware changes are needed for this reference.
Review existing practice tasks for contradictions; report proposed corrections to root rather than editing shared practice files.
